self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop shows the ready-hold, a lane flicking green, and the hand slapping it fast (a speed burst), then the hand tapping too early and a red false-start buzzer. One unscored warm-up start precedes the scored block.

learning_science.why: Choice reaction time grows linearly with log2(number of alternatives), and that slope indexes central information-processing rate more cleanly than absolute RT.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Offer 1/2/4 lanes as a difficulty lever and derive the RT-vs-log2(N) slope (M-HICKSLOPE) so the intercept absorbs motor/device latency.
learning_science.source: Hick, W. E. (1952). On the rate of gain of information. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 4(1), 11-26.

learning_science.why: Intra-individual RT variability and lapses predict ability better than mean or fastest RT.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score RT variability (CV) and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) and never credit peak speed.
learning_science.source: Larson, G. E., & Alderton, D. L. (1990). Reaction time variability and intelligence: A worst performance analysis of individual differences. Intelligence, 14(3), 309-325.

learning_science.why: Responses before the signal are guesses, not perception, so impulsive early taps must never be rewarded.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Flag taps under 150 ms and any pre-signal tap as false starts that break the streak and are excluded from RT (M-FALSEALARM).
learning_science.source: Luce, R. D. (1986). Response Times: Their Role in Inferring Elementary Mental Organization. Oxford University Press.

tail_precision_rationale: Peak reaction time is famously weak and device-confounded, so this type deliberately scores the parts of the RT distribution that do track ability: intra-individual variability and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE; worst-performance rule) and the Hick slope (M-HICKSLOPE), whose intercept absorbs motor/device latency so the slope is a cleaner central-rate estimate. Choice trials are credited only when the correct lane is hit (M-SPEEDACC) and anticipations are flagged (M-FALSEALARM), so fast-wrong is never rewarded. Standalone tail power is modest and framed as one converging, engagement-gated signal.
age_rationale: Slapping a lit pad is the most motor-basic speeded act, so simple RT (one GO pad) fits K-1 with a huge target. Choice RT (two then four lanes) is layered for 2-3 through 6-8 to derive the Hick slope. Pad size is held constant across bands to control the motor (Fitts) confound; K-1 uses simple RT only.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 one GO pad (simple RT) -> 2-3 two lanes (2-choice) -> 4-5 two to four lanes -> 6-8 four lanes with a short deadline and catch (no-signal) starts
adaptive.difficulty_levers: number of lanes (Hick N), ready-hold jitter, response deadline, proportion of catch (no-signal) trials
adaptive.notes: Trials are fully parametric (N, ready-hold, deadline); the RT-vs-log2(N) slope is computed across blocks and start-line stimuli are trivially cloneable.

engagement_hook: A drag-race start line: coiled anticipation, slam the lane the instant it goes green, and jumping early is a false start - cool, precise timing wins the streak.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Anticipatory false starts (flagged <150 ms and pre-signal); device input latency (report variability and the Hick slope, whose intercept absorbs device/motor latency); touch vs mouse differences; fatigue on long blocks (drift/engagement logged); large pads limit the Fitts motor confound.

name: Coin Drop
topics_techniques_covered: simple_reaction_time: a coin is released after a jittered hold and the child taps CATCH the instant it starts to fall (a ruler-drop-style reaction to motion onset), over many trials recording mean and especially the variability of response time
choice_reaction_time: the coin tips toward one of two then four chutes and the child taps the chute it falls into, a fast low-reading choice reaction whose time rises with the number of chutes

choice_reaction_time: reaction across 1, 2 and 4 chutes so the slope of response time against log2(number of choices) indexes processing rate (Hick's law) with the motor/device intercept separated out
simple_reaction_time: derive intra-individual RT variability and lapse frequency from the drop block; per the worst-performance rule the slowest catches, not the fastest, carry the ability signal
one_liner: A coin hangs at the top and drops without warning; the child catches it the instant it falls - or taps the chute it tips into.
interaction: A coin is held at the top. After a jittered hold it is released and begins to fall; the child taps the large CATCH pad the instant motion begins (simple), or taps the chute (two or four) the coin tips toward (choice). A tap before release is a false start (flagged, excluded from RT); letting it hit the floor is a miss. Brief feedback, then the next drop. Tapping only.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop shows the coin drop and a fast catch (the coin banked), then a too-early tap and a red false-start. One unscored warm-up drop precedes the scored block.

learning_science.why: Choice reaction time rises linearly with log2(number of alternatives), and that slope indexes information-processing rate with the motor/device latency isolated in the intercept.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Offer 1/2/4 chutes and derive the RT-vs-log2(N) slope (M-HICKSLOPE) as a device-robust rate estimate.
learning_science.source: Hick, W. E. (1952). On the rate of gain of information. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 4(1), 11-26.

learning_science.why: A child's slowest responses correlate with ability more strongly than their fastest, so consistency beats peak speed.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Report RT variability and slow-tail lapse frequency (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) on correct catches rather than best or mean RT.
learning_science.source: Coyle, T. R. (2003). A review of the worst performance rule. Intelligence, 31(6), 567-587.

learning_science.why: A drop task invites jumping the gun, so pre-release taps and impulsive fast-wrong chute choices must not be rewarded.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Flag responses under 150 ms and any pre-release tap as false starts (M-FALSEALARM) and credit choice RT only when the correct chute is hit (M-SPEEDACC).
learning_science.source: Wickelgren, W. A. (1977). Speed-accuracy tradeoff and information processing dynamics. Acta Psychologica, 41(1), 67-85.

tail_precision_rationale: Motion-onset catch time is a classic but weak, motor- and device-bound signal, so scoring leans on the ability-linked parts of the RT distribution: intra-individual variability and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE; worst-performance rule) and the Hick slope (M-HICKSLOPE) whose intercept absorbs device/motor latency. Anticipatory catches are flagged (M-FALSEALARM) and choice catches are credited only when correct (M-SPEEDACC), so fast-wrong is never rewarded. It is one modest, engagement-gated converging signal, not a standalone tail decider.
age_rationale: Catching a falling coin on motion onset is motor-basic, so simple RT fits K-1 with a huge CATCH pad. Choice RT (two then four chutes) is layered for 2-3 through 6-8 to derive the Hick slope. Pad/chute size is held constant across bands to control the Fitts confound; K-1 uses simple catch only.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 one CATCH pad (simple RT) -> 2-3 two chutes (2-choice) -> 4-5 two to four chutes -> 6-8 four chutes with a short floor deadline and catch (no-drop) trials
adaptive.difficulty_levers: number of chutes (Hick N), release-hold jitter, fall speed / floor deadline, proportion of no-drop catch trials
adaptive.notes: Drops are fully parametric (N, hold, fall speed); the RT-vs-log2(N) slope is computed across blocks and the falling stimulus is trivially cloneable.

engagement_hook: Catch the falling treasure the instant it drops - too eager (a pre-release tap) is a false start, so steady, precise timing banks the streak.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Anticipatory false starts (flagged <150 ms and pre-release); fall rendering depends on device frame rate (report variability and the Hick slope whose intercept absorbs device/motor latency); touch vs mouse differences; fatigue (drift/engagement logged); large pads/chutes limit the Fitts motor confound.

name: Critter Watch
topics_techniques_covered: sustained_attention_vigilance: a continuous-performance watch (TOVA/Conners-style) where friendly targets appear frequently and a rare intruder must be withheld, scoring RT, RT variability, omissions and commissions over a multi-minute block
symbol_search: each item requires detecting and confirming whether the presented creature is the target among confusable foils before responding, a serial target-detection search in time
perceptual_speed: a rapid same/different discrimination of each item against the held target at a steady fast cadence (a Pattern-Comparison-style perceptual-speed component)
sustained_attention_vigilance: intra-individual RT variability and lapse timing across the block index attentional stability rather than peak speed (worst-performance rule)
one_liner: Friendly critters pop up one after another; the child taps every friendly one fast but must freeze and not tap the rare grumpy intruder.
interaction: One creature appears at a time in the center at a steady beat. The child taps a large pad for a frequent friendly target and withholds (does nothing) for the rare intruder. Each item auto-advances after a short window; hits, misses (omissions) and wrong taps on an intruder (commissions) are logged. Tapping only; the block runs for many trials to expose the vigilance decrement.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop taps two friendly critters (a combo ticks up) then visibly freezes and pulls back on a grumpy intruder (a green 'good freeze'). One unscored warm-up with one target and one intruder precedes scoring.

learning_science.why: Sustained target detection with occasional withholding is the canonical measure of vigilance and attentional stability, which processing-speed subtests and CogAT omit.
learning_science.concrete_decision: A frequent-target / rare-no-go stream over a multi-minute block scoring omissions, commissions, RT and RT variability.
learning_science.source: Rosvold, H. E., Mirsky, A. F., Sarason, I., Bransome, E. D., & Beck, L. H. (1956). A continuous performance test of brain damage. Journal of Consulting Psychology, 20(5), 343-350.

learning_science.why: Hits and false alarms must be separated from response bias so a cautious child and an impulsive guesser are not scored alike.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Compute d-prime from hits and false alarms across target and no-go trials (M-DPRIME) and score commissions (M-COMM, M-FALSEALARM).
learning_science.source: Green, D. M., & Swets, J. A. (1966). Signal Detection Theory and Psychophysics. Wiley.

learning_science.why: Low intra-individual RT variability and few lapses mark strong attenders better than peak speed.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Emphasize RT CV and slow-tail lapses on hits (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) and never credit raw speed.
learning_science.source: Larson, G. E., & Alderton, D. L. (1990). Reaction time variability and intelligence. Intelligence, 14(3), 309-325.

tail_precision_rationale: A vigilance/CPT stream barely separates the gifted tail on speed, so scoring leans on attentional stability (low RT variability and few slow-tail lapses; M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE), commission control that isolates impulsive fast-wrong responding (M-COMM, M-FALSEALARM), signal-detection sensitivity that removes response bias (M-DPRIME), and drift (M-DRIFT) that certifies sustained, engaged performance. Speed is never credited on an intruder, so fast-wrong is never rewarded; the type's real value is a consistency plus collateral-engagement read, with low standalone tail discrimination.
age_rationale: At K-1 it runs as a short, high-target-rate detection watch with distinct, concrete creatures and a very low, forgiving intruder rate, so it works mainly as target detection plus a basic sustained watch (withholding is developmentally immature that young). Rare-no-go withholding, confusable foils, and longer low-event blocks that expose the vigilance decrement are layered in from 2-3 to 6-8. Content and block length, not motor demand, set the band.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 friendly animals, high target rate, rare and obvious intruder, short block -> 2-3 clearer no-go withholding -> 4-5 more confusable foils, longer block -> 6-8 confusable creatures, higher no-go rate, multi-minute block
adaptive.difficulty_levers: target:no-go ratio, presentation cadence, foil similarity, block length (vigilance decrement), response window
adaptive.notes: The stream is generated from a target/foil pool with a controlled no-go rate; d-prime, commissions and omissions score automatically and unlimited matched streams can be cloned.

engagement_hook: A tap-the-friendlies watch with a 'good freeze' reward for holding back on the rare grumpy intruder - a calm, steady streak beats trigger-happy tapping.
construct_irrelevant_risks: A motor tapping-speed floor; withholding is immature at K-1 (low, forgiving no-go rate there); device input latency (report RT variability and d-prime over raw speed); the vigilance decrement is expected and logged as drift, not scored as ability; reading is avoided with picture creatures.

name: Meadow Windows
topics_techniques_covered: sustained_attention_vigilance: a spatially distributed watch where a target briefly peeks from a random window among several and must be caught while foil peeks are ignored, sustained over a multi-minute block scoring hits, omissions, commissions and RT variability

symbol_search: on each event the child must locate which window shows the target among distractor windows, a spatial target-detection search whose difficulty scales with window count and foil similarity
perceptual_speed: a rapid discrimination of target versus foil at the popped window (a speeded perceptual comparison component)
sustained_attention_vigilance: RT variability and lapse timing across the block index attentional stability rather than peak speed
one_liner: Little windows dot a meadow; every so often a target peeks out of one and the child taps that window fast, ignoring the pesky look-alikes.
interaction: Several windows are shown. At jittered intervals a creature peeks from one window: a target (tap that window) or a foil (withhold). The peek is brief; tapping the target window is a hit, tapping a foil peek or an empty window is a false alarm, and a missed target is an omission. The block runs for many events to expose the vigilance decrement. Tapping only.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop taps a target peeking from one window (a pop of confetti), then withholds on a foil peek at another window. One unscored warm-up with one target peek and one foil peek precedes scoring.

learning_science.why: Sustained monitoring for infrequent, spatially distributed signals degrades over time, and that decline is itself an attention signal.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Run a multi-minute block and log accuracy/RT drift across it (M-DRIFT), discounting disengaged late events rather than scoring them as ability.
learning_science.source: Mackworth, N. H. (1948). The breakdown of vigilance during prolonged visual search. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 1(1), 6-21.

learning_science.why: Spatial hits versus false alarms must be separated from a tap-happy response bias.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Compute d-prime and the commission/false-alarm rate across target and foil peeks (M-DPRIME, M-FALSEALARM).
learning_science.source: Green, D. M., & Swets, J. A. (1966). Signal Detection Theory and Psychophysics. Wiley.

learning_science.why: Finding which window shows the target is a spatial search whose difficulty scales with the number of windows and foil similarity.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Scale window count and target-foil similarity as difficulty levers and log the tap-location path (M-PATH).
learning_science.source: Treisman, A., & Gelade, G. (1980). A feature-integration theory of attention. Cognitive Psychology, 12(1), 97-136.

tail_precision_rationale: Spatial vigilance is a weak tail signal on speed, so scoring leans on signal-detection sensitivity that removes tap-happy bias (M-DPRIME), false-alarm control (M-FALSEALARM), attentional stability (RT variability and few slow-tail lapses; M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE), and drift (M-DRIFT) that certifies sustained engagement. Speed is never credited on a foil peek, so fast-wrong is never rewarded; the type is a consistency plus collateral-engagement read with low standalone tail discrimination.
age_rationale: Tapping the window a target peeks from is motor-simple, so it spans K-1 (two large windows, a distinct target, high peek rate, few obvious foils) to 6-8 (up to six windows, confusable foils, a longer low-event block). Window count and foil similarity, not motor demand, set the band; large windows control the Fitts confound and picture targets avoid reading.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 two windows, distinct target, high peek rate -> 2-3 three to four windows -> 4-5 four to five windows, moderate foils -> 6-8 six windows, confusable foils, multi-minute block
adaptive.difficulty_levers: number of windows, peek duration, target:foil ratio, foil similarity, block length
adaptive.notes: Events are generated from a target/foil pool with a controlled foil rate and a known target window, so d-prime and commissions score automatically and unlimited matched blocks can be cloned.

engagement_hook: A peek-a-boo meadow watch - pounce on the target the instant it peeks from a window, but ignore the look-alikes; a clean-catch streak rewards patience.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Screen size limits window count; motor tap speed and accuracy (mitigated by large windows and constant spacing); reading avoided with picture targets; false alarms penalized via d-prime and the commission rate; the vigilance decrement is expected and logged as drift, not scored as ability.

name: Twin Lane Watch
topics_techniques_covered: sustained_attention_vigilance: a divided-attention watch over two simultaneous lanes where a target may appear in either lane and must be caught while non-targets are ignored, sustained over a multi-minute block scoring hits, omissions, commissions and RT variability
symbol_search: on each event the child must search both lanes to detect whether and where the target appeared, a dual-channel target-detection search
sustained_attention_vigilance: RT variability and lapse timing across the divided block index attentional stability under load rather than peak speed
one_liner: Two lanes run at once and the child must watch both, tapping the lane where a target shows up while ignoring everything else.
interaction: Two lanes run side by side. Items appear in each lane on independent jittered schedules; when a target appears in a lane the child taps that lane and ignores non-targets. Hits, omissions and false alarms are logged per lane; the block runs for many events. Tapping only, one large pad per lane.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop taps a target in the left lane, then a target in the right lane, and withholds on a non-target. One unscored warm-up event in each lane precedes scoring.

learning_science.why: Monitoring two channels at once taxes attentional capacity beyond single-stream vigilance, exposing capacity limits a single stream misses.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Two independent lanes force divided monitoring; per-lane hit rate and RT are compared to a single-lane baseline to index the divided-attention cost.
learning_science.source: Kahneman, D. (1973). Attention and Effort. Prentice-Hall.

learning_science.why: Lapses and RT variability during sustained responding index attentional stability more than mean speed.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score RT variability and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) and drift across the block (M-DRIFT) rather than peak speed.
learning_science.source: Robertson, I. H., Manly, T., Andrade, J., Baddeley, B. T., & Yiend, J. (1997). 'Oops!': Performance correlates of everyday attentional failures in normal and traumatically brain-injured subjects. Neuropsychologia, 35(6), 747-758.

learning_science.why: Hits versus false alarms across two channels must be separated from response bias.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Compute d-prime and the false-alarm rate over target and non-target events (M-DPRIME, M-FALSEALARM).
learning_science.source: Green, D. M., & Swets, J. A. (1966). Signal Detection Theory and Psychophysics. Wiley.

tail_precision_rationale: Divided-attention watch speed is a weak tail signal, so scoring leans on signal-detection sensitivity (M-DPRIME), false-alarm control (M-FALSEALARM), attentional stability under load (RT variability and few slow-tail lapses; M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE), and drift (M-DRIFT) that certifies sustained engagement. Speed is never credited on a non-target, so fast-wrong is never rewarded; the type is a consistency plus collateral-engagement read with low standalone tail discrimination.
age_rationale: Tapping the lane where a target appears is motor-simple. At K-1 it runs slowly with two lanes and a distinct, high-rate target, so it works mainly as a gentle two-lane target-detection watch; faster cadence, confusable non-targets, and a longer divided-attention block are layered in from 2-3 to 6-8. Cadence and foil similarity, not motor demand, set the band.

adaptive.content_range: K-1 two lanes, slow cadence, distinct high-rate target -> 2-3 moderate cadence -> 4-5 faster, more confusable non-targets -> 6-8 fast cadence, confusable non-targets, multi-minute divided block
adaptive.difficulty_levers: presentation cadence, target:non-target ratio, foil similarity, block length, single-lane vs dual-lane baseline
adaptive.notes: Each lane is an independently generated stream from a target/foil pool with a controlled target rate, so per-lane d-prime and false alarms score automatically and unlimited matched blocks can be cloned.

engagement_hook: Keep both lanes in view at once and pounce on a target wherever it pops - a divided-attention watch where a steady, clean streak beats frantic tapping.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Divided attention is demanding, so K-1 runs slow and gentle (treated as basic detection plus engagement); motor tap speed (large lane pads); device latency (report variability and d-prime over raw speed); non-target false alarms penalized; the decrement across the block is logged as drift, not scored as ability; reading avoided with picture targets.

name: Message Decoder
topics_techniques_covered: symbol_coding: a decode-the-message game - using a shown symbol-to-letter/digit legend, translate a coded sequence of symbols into the hidden word by tapping each decoded output in order, decoding as many messages as possible before time runs out
coding_digit_symbol: using a fixed visible key pairing each symbol with a digit/letter, produce the matching output for each presented symbol under time, scored on correct decisions per unit time
symbol_coding: the legend is refreshed each block so the score reflects speeded substitution rather than memorized pairs
coding_digit_symbol: scrolling symbol-to-output substitution scoring correct matches and average time per correct match
one_liner: A secret message of symbols appears with a legend; the child decodes it symbol by symbol, tapping each letter to spell the hidden word before time runs out.
interaction: A fixed legend (symbol -> letter/digit) sits on screen. A short coded message (a row of symbols) is shown with the current symbol highlighted; the child taps the decoded output on a response keypad. A correct tap fills that slot and advances to the next symbol; a wrong tap flashes red and stays until corrected. Finishing a message loads the next. Tapping only; the legend stays visible.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop traces from the highlighted symbol up to the legend, then taps the matching letter on the keypad (the slot fills). One unscored warm-up symbol with the legend row highlighted precedes the timed block.

learning_science.principle: Digit-Symbol / Coding as a processing-speed marker
learning_science.why: Symbol substitution under time is a long-validated index of clerical/processing speed in child batteries.
learning_science.concrete_decision: A fixed visible legend, decode messages, and score correct outputs per unit time plus per-symbol consistency.
learning_science.source: Wechsler, D. (2014). WISC-V Technical and Interpretive Manual (Coding / Processing Speed Index). Pearson.

learning_science.why: Consistency of substitution speed tracks ability better than the single fastest decode.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Emphasize inter-symbol time variability and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) on correct decodes rather than peak decode speed.
learning_science.source: Coyle, T. R. (2003). A review of the worst performance rule. Intelligence, 31(6), 567-587.

learning_science.why: Looking between a distant legend and the message adds load unrelated to speed, so a novel child may fail for layout reasons.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Keep the legend, message and keypad on one screen and teach the look-up via a ghost-hand plus one warm-up.
learning_science.source: Chandler, P., & Sweller, J. (1992). The split-attention effect as a factor in the design of instruction. British Journal of Educational Psychology, 62(2), 233-246.

tail_precision_rationale: Decode throughput is coachable and weak alone, so the sharper signals are substitution consistency (M-RTVAR) and slow-tail lapses (M-LAPSE) on correct decodes, plus the accuracy-gated speed-accuracy point (M-SPEEDACC) and revisions before commit (M-REV). Randomizing the legend each block blunts practice inflation and a wrong decode must be corrected, so fast-wrong is never rewarded. Its tail value is corroborating efficiency and engagement evidence, not a primary separator.
age_rationale: Decoding a sequence requires holding a legend and cross-referencing, so it starts at 2-3 (3-4 picture-symbol pairs, short 2-3 symbol messages) and extends to 6-8 (full 1-9 key, longer messages). K-1 is excluded because sequence cross-referencing, not perceptual speed, would dominate and unfairly penalize kindergarteners, whose coding speed is captured by tap-select and matching types.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 short messages, 3-4 picture-symbol pairs -> 4-5 six digit-symbol pairs, medium messages -> 6-8 full 1-9 key, longer messages
adaptive.difficulty_levers: legend size (number of pairs), symbol confusability, message length, legend always-visible vs briefly hidden (adds working memory), time budget
adaptive.notes: Legend mappings are randomized per block (anti-practice) and correct/incorrect is deterministic from the legend, so parallel forms are unlimited.

engagement_hook: A spy 'crack the secret word' race against a shrinking timer, with a decoded-messages counter and a clean-decode combo for fast correct symbols.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Split-attention/layout load if legend and message are far apart (kept adjacent); symbol confusability and fine targets (large keypad used); practice with a fixed legend (randomized per block); reading is limited to letter/digit recognition and digits can be used for pre-readers.

name: Decoder Ring
topics_techniques_covered: symbol_coding: a decoder-ring game - a cipher wheel shows the symbol-to-output legend; for each presented symbol the child rotates the ring to bring the matching output under the pointer and locks it, decoding as many as possible before time runs out
coding_digit_symbol: using the fixed visible key on the wheel, produce the output paired with each presented symbol under time, scored on correct decisions per unit time
symbol_coding: the wheel mapping is reshuffled each block so the score reflects speeded substitution rather than memorized pairs
one_liner: A spy decoder ring shows the code; for each symbol the child spins the ring to line up the matching letter under the pointer and locks it in.
interaction: A cipher wheel (an outer ring of symbols aligned to an inner ring of outputs) is shown as the legend. A prompt symbol appears in a window; the child taps rotate-left / rotate-right (or drags) to bring the matching output under a fixed pointer, then taps LOCK. A correct lock advances; a wrong lock flashes red and can be corrected. Rotating and tapping only; the wheel stays visible.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop shows the prompt symbol, the hand nudging the wheel until the matching output sits under the pointer, then tapping LOCK (a checkmark). One unscored warm-up decode precedes the timed block.

learning_science.principle: Digit-Symbol / Coding as a processing-speed marker
learning_science.why: Symbol-to-output cross-referencing under time is a long-validated index of clerical/processing speed in child batteries.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Keep a fixed visible key on the wheel and score correct decodes per unit time plus decode consistency.
learning_science.source: Wechsler, D. (2014). WISC-V Technical and Interpretive Manual (Coding / Processing Speed Index). Pearson.

learning_science.why: Consistency of substitution speed tracks ability better than the single fastest decode.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Emphasize inter-decode time variability and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) on correct decodes rather than peak speed.
learning_science.source: Coyle, T. R. (2003). A review of the worst performance rule. Intelligence, 31(6), 567-587.

learning_science.why: Rotating a dial adds a graduated motor component that can confound a pure speed estimate.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use discrete rotate steps and a large wheel, score decode identity not rotation smoothness, and report consistency and over-rotations (M-REV) rather than raw speed.
learning_science.source: Fitts, P. M. (1954). The information capacity of the human motor system in controlling the amplitude of movement. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 47(6), 381-391.

tail_precision_rationale: Decode throughput on a dial is motor-confounded and coachable, so tail value rests on decode consistency (M-RTVAR) and slow-tail lapses (M-LAPSE) on correct decodes, few over-rotations (M-REV), and the accuracy-gated speed-accuracy point (M-SPEEDACC), with drift (M-DRIFT) gating engagement. The wheel mapping is reshuffled each block to blunt practice and a wrong lock must be corrected, so fast-wrong is never rewarded. It is collateral efficiency/engagement evidence, explicitly not a standalone tail separator.
age_rationale: Rotating a dial to align an output adds a fine-motor and spatial-mapping demand absent from tap-select coding, so it starts at 4-5 where that control is adequate (large wheel, discrete rotate buttons, 4-6 pairs) and extends to 6-8 (full key, finer steps, confusable symbols). K-1 and 2-3 are excluded because rotary control and cross-referencing would swamp the speed signal; their coding speed is captured by tap-select and sort types.

adaptive.content_range: 4-5 small wheel, 4-6 pairs, discrete rotate buttons -> 6-8 full 1-9 key, finer rotation, more confusable symbols
adaptive.difficulty_levers: key size, rotation granularity (discrete steps vs free drag), symbol confusability, time budget
adaptive.notes: Wheel mappings are reshuffled per block (anti-practice) and decode identity is deterministic from the key, so parallel forms are unlimited.

engagement_hook: A secret-agent decoder ring - spin the wheel to crack each symbol, with a decode counter climbing and a clean-lock combo for fast correct decodes.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Rotary fine-motor and spatial mapping (mitigated by discrete rotate steps, a large wheel, scoring decode identity not rotation smoothness, and reporting consistency and over-rotations over raw speed); split-attention (the wheel is the legend, kept on screen); practice with a fixed mapping (reshuffled per block); excluded from the youngest bands where motor demand would dominate.

name: Symbol Sort
topics_techniques_covered: symbol_coding: a sort-the-mail coding game - a legend maps each symbol to a labeled bin and the child taps the correct bin for each incoming symbol per the legend, sorting as many as possible before time runs out
coding_digit_symbol: using the fixed visible key, route each presented symbol to its keyed output bin under time, scored on correct decisions per unit time
symbol_coding: bin assignments are reshuffled each block so the score reflects speeded substitution rather than memorized pairs
one_liner: Symbols arrive one at a time and the child taps the bin each one belongs to, sorting the mail as fast as they can using the legend.
interaction: A legend pairs each symbol with a labeled bin (a digit or color). A symbol appears at the top; the child taps the bin it belongs to per the legend. A correct tap sends it to that bin and advances; a wrong tap flashes red and is logged as a mis-route. As many symbols as possible are sorted before the timer ends. Tapping only; the legend and bins stay visible.
self_teach: A <=10s wordless ghost-hand loop shows a symbol, the hand tracing to the legend then tapping the matching bin (the symbol drops in). One unscored warm-up symbol precedes the timed block.

learning_science.principle: Digit-Symbol / Coding as a processing-speed marker
learning_science.why: Routing symbols to keyed outputs under time is a long-validated clerical/processing-speed task.
learning_science.concrete_decision: A fixed visible legend, route each symbol to its bin, and score correct routes per unit time plus routing consistency.
learning_science.source: Wechsler, D. (2014). WISC-V Technical and Interpretive Manual (Coding / Processing Speed Index). Pearson.

learning_science.why: Consistency of routing speed tracks ability better than the single fastest route.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Emphasize inter-route time variability and slow-tail lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) on correct routes rather than peak speed.
learning_science.source: Coyle, T. R. (2003). A review of the worst performance rule. Intelligence, 31(6), 567-587.

learning_science.why: Looking between a distant legend and the bins adds load unrelated to speed.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Keep the legend, symbol and bins on one screen and teach the look-up via a ghost-hand plus one warm-up; mis-routes are penalized so speed is credited only when accurate (M-FALSEALARM, M-SPEEDACC).
learning_science.source: Chandler, P., & Sweller, J. (1992). The split-attention effect as a factor in the design of instruction. British Journal of Educational Psychology, 62(2), 233-246.

tail_precision_rationale: Sort throughput is coachable and weak alone, so the sharper signals are routing consistency (M-RTVAR) and slow-tail lapses (M-LAPSE) on correct routes, mis-route control that isolates impulsive fast-wrong routing (M-FALSEALARM), and the accuracy-gated speed-accuracy point (M-SPEEDACC), with drift (M-DRIFT) gating engagement. Bin assignments are reshuffled per block to blunt practice; a mis-route is never rewarded. Its tail value is corroborating efficiency and engagement evidence, not a primary separator.
age_rationale: Routing a symbol to a labeled bin requires holding a legend and cross-referencing, so it starts at 2-3 (two-three bins, picture symbols) and extends to 6-8 (many bins, confusable symbols). K-1 is excluded because multi-bin cross-referencing, not perceptual speed, would dominate; K-1 speed is captured by matching and sweep types.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 two-three bins, picture symbols -> 4-5 four bins -> 6-8 many bins, confusable symbols
adaptive.difficulty_levers: number of bins, symbol confusability, incoming rate / time budget, legend always-visible vs briefly hidden
adaptive.notes: Bin assignments are reshuffled per block (anti-practice) and correct/incorrect is deterministic from the legend, so parallel forms and mis-route keys are unlimited.

engagement_hook: A sort-the-mail race - fling each symbol into its bin as fast as you can, with a sorted-count meter and a clean-sort combo while a wrong bin shakes.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Split-attention/layout load if legend and bins are far apart (kept adjacent); mis-routes are penalized so fast-wrong is never rewarded; symbol confusability and target size (large bins used); practice with a fixed legend (reshuffled per block); reading is limited to digit/picture recognition.
